newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL Mutual Fund says sees profit recovery in 1997.
newsitem.headline: KL Mutual Fund says sees profit recovery in 1997.

text.p: The Kuala Lumpur Mutual Fund Bhd, a subsidiary of Public Bank Bhd, said its performance was expected to recover this year from the sharp fall in profits last year.
Its chairman Mohamed Nizam Abdul Razak told reporters after Public Bank's annual general meeting that the launch of new funds and products was expected to help it report higher profit.
"I'll attribute it to greater competition," he said, when asked why the mutual fund firm's profit had declined by 274 percent to 20.9 million ringgit in 1996 from the year before.
He said the government's policy of encouraging asset management had brought in many more companies into the business last year, which had attracted some money from KL Mutual's funds.
"We have put in place measures which will stop that this year," Nizam said.
He said there were more redemptions from the company's various funds compared with last year. "But, sales have been very encouraging compared with last year," he said.
